{{nihongo|'''Shinaga Shrine'''|科長神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Kawachi Province]].

'''Shinaga Shrine''' (しながじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|arz|تايشى|ca|Taishi (Osaka)|eo|Taishi (Osako)|es|Taishi (Osaka)|fa|تایشی، اوساکا|fr|Taishi (Osaka)|hy|Տայսի|it|Taishi (Osaka)|ja|太子町 (大阪府)|ko|다이시정 (오사카부)|ms|Taishi, Osaka|pl|Taishi (Osaka)|ru|Тайси (Осака)|sv|Taishi, Osaka|tl|Taishi, Osaka|tr|Taishi, Osaka|uk|Тайші (Осака)|ur|تائیشی، اوساکا|zh|太子町 (大阪府)|qid=Q1347173|lt=Taishi}}, {{ill|Minamikawachi District, Osaka|ar|محافظة ميناميكاواشي (أوساكا)|arz|محافظه ميناميكاواشى, اوساكا|ca|Districte de Minamikawachi|ceb|Minamikawachi-gun|de|Minamikawachi-gun|eo|Distrikto Minamikawachi|es|Distrito de Minamikawachi|fr|District de Minamikawachi|id|Distrik Minamikawachi, Ōsaka|it|Distretto di Minamikawachi|ja|南河内郡|ko|미나미카와치군|lt|Minamikavačio apskritis|pl|Powiat Minamikawachi|sr|Област Минамикавачи|uk|Повіт Мінамі-Кавачі|zh|南河內郡|qid=Q1347323}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|Q122723|qid=Q122723}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}}, and its former {{ill|Shakaku|ja|社格|ko|사격 (신토)|zh|社格|qid=Q10444029}} was {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}.

===Enshrined deities===
Its principal deities are the wind deities {{ill|Shinatsuhiko|Q1073925|qid=Q1073925|lt=Shinatsuhiko-no-Mikoto and Shinatsuhime-no-Mikoto}}. The following are associated or merged deities:
* Associated -- {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|Q272993|qid=Q272993|lt=Susanoo-no-Mikoto}}, {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|Q317997|qid=Q317997|qid=Q317997|lt=Hondawake-no-Mikoto}}, {{ill|Takeminakata|es|Takeminakata|hu|Takeminakata|id|Takeminakata|ja|タケミナカタ|mni|ꯇꯀꯦꯃꯤꯅꯀꯇ|pl|Takeminakata|zh|建御名方神|qid=Q9150391|lt=Takeminakata-no-Mikoto}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|de|Takemikazuchi|eo|Takemikazuĉi|es|Takemikazuchi|fa|تاکه‌میکازوچی|fr|Takemikazuchi|id|Takemikazuchi|ja|タケミカヅチ|pl|Takemikazuchi|pt|Takemikadzuchi|ru|Такэмикадзути|zh|建御雷|qid=Q1502690|lt=Takemikazuchi-no-Mikoto}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|fr|Futsunushi|it|Futsunushi|ja|経津主神|mni|ꯐꯨꯠꯁꯨꯅꯨꯁꯤ|pl|Futsunushi|ru|Фуцунуси|zh|經津主神|qid=Q1107286|lt=Futsunushi-no-Mikoto}}, {{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|Q2564508|qid=Q2564508|lt=Ame-no-Koyane-no-Mikoto}}, {{ill|Amaterasu|Q455602|qid=Q455602}}
* Merged -- {{ill|Tatsuta Taisha|Q246455|qid=Q246455|lt=Ame no Mihashira and Kuni no Mihashira Ōkami}}, Ame-no-Koyane-no-Mikoto, Hondawake-no-Mikoto, Yasaka Ōkami, Dōso Ōkami, {{ill|Ukemochi|Q2280323|qid=Q2280323}}, {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|Q382005|qid=Q382005}}, {{ill|Ichikishima-hime|fr|Ichikishimahime|ja|イチキシマヒメ|simple|Ichikishima-hime|zh|市寸島比賣命|qid=Q11059454|lt=Ichikishimahime-no-Mikoto}}, Amaterasu Ōmikami

===History===
Its founding origin is unknown. Originally it stood on {{ill|Mount Nijō|arz|نيجو سان|ceb|Nijō San|fr|Mont Nijō|ja|二上山 (奈良県・大阪府)|lld|Mont Nijō|qid=Q11371271|lt=Mount Nijō}} and was called '''Nijō Gongen'''. In the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}, it is listed as “Shinaga Shrine, {{ill|Ishikawa district|ja|石川郡 (大阪府)|zh|石川郡 (大阪府)|qid=Q11586399|lt=Ishikawa District}}, {{ill|Kawachi Province|Q1047150|qid=Q1047150}},” and ranked as a small shrine. In {{ill|Ryakunin|fa|ریاکونین|fr|Ère Ryakunin|ia|Ryakunin|id|Ryakunin|ja|暦仁|ko|랴쿠닌|ru|Рякунин|simple|Ryakunin|sr|Рјакунин|tr|Ryakunin|uk|Рякунін|zh|曆仁|qid=Q1193948}} 1 ({{ill|1238|ab|1238|af|1238|als|1238|am|1238 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1238|ar|1238|ary|1238|arz|1238|ast|1238|avk|1238|az|1238|azb|۱۲۳۸ (میلادی)|be|1238|be_x_old|1238|bg|1238|bn|১২৩৮|bpy|মারি ১২৩৮|br|1238|bs|1238.|ca|1238|cdo|1238 nièng|ceb|1238|ckb|١٢٣٨|crh|1238|cs|1238|csb|1238|cv|1238|cy|1238|da|1238|de|1238|diq|1238|el|1238|eml|1238|eo|1238|es|1238|et|1238|eu|1238|fa|۱۲۳۸ (میلادی)|fi|1238|fo|1238|fr|1238|frr|1238|fy|1238|ga|1238|gan|1238年|gcr|1238|gd|1238|gl|1238|he|1238|hi|१२३८|hr|1238.|ht|1238 (almanak jilyen)|hu|1238|hy|1238|id|1238|ilo|1238|io|1238|is|1238|it|1238|ja|1238年|jv|1238|ka|1238|kaa|1238|kk|1238 жыл|ko|1238년|la|1238|lb|1238|lij|1238|lmo|1238|lt|1238 m.|lv|1238. gads|map_bms|1238|mdf|1238|mg|1238|mhr|1238|mi|1238|min|1238|mk|1238|mr|इ.स. १२३८|mrj|1238 и|ms|1238|my|၁၂၃၈|mzn|۱۲۳۸|nah|1238|nap|1238|nds|1238|new|सन् १२३८|nl|1238|nn|1238|no|1238|nrm|1238|nso|1238|oc|1238|or|୧୨୩୮|os|1238-æм аз|pl|1238|pnb|1238|pt|1238|qu|1238|ro|1238|ru|1238 год|rue|1238|sa|१२३८|sah|1238|scn|1238|sd|1238ع|se|1238|sh|1238.|shn|1238|simple|1238|sk|1238|sl|1238|smn|1238|sq|1238|sr|1238|su|1238|sv|1238|sw|1238|tg|Соли 1238|th|พ.ศ. 1781|tk|1238|tl|1238|tly|1238|tr|1238|tt|1238 ел|uk|1238|ur|1238ء|uz|1238|vec|1238|vi|1238|war|1238|wuu|1238年|xmf|1238|yo|1238|zh|1238年|zh_min_nan|1238 nî|zh_yue|1238年|qid=Q5433}}), it was moved to its current location. There had originally been an Ebisu Shrine (also called Tsuchi-so Shrine) at the current site, and tradition says it became a {{ill|Massha|ja|末社|qid=Q135009906}} when Shinaga Shrine moved there.

Until the Edo period it was called '''Hassha Daimyōjin'''. ''Shikinaisha Chōsa Hōkoku'' states: “When {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Fujiwara no Yoritaka}} moved Nijō Gongen to the current site, he invited and merged Kasuga deities, ancestral gods of the Fujiwara clan, and likely suppressed the old name Shinaga Shrine and called it Hassha Daimyōjin.”

There is also a tradition that this was the birthplace of {{ill|Empress Jingū|Q232803|qid=Q232803}}, and among shrine treasures is a model helmet said to have been used by her. ''Shikinaisha Chōsa Hōkoku'' notes that “Shinaga may have shifted from Shinaga -> Isanaga -> Okinaga, giving rise to the Empress Jingū birthplace legend from the Okinaga lineage.”

It was ranked as gōsha on April 1, Meiji 5, and designated as a shinsen-heihaku offering shrine on January 28, Meiji 40. In Meiji 40, nearby Shinagaoka Shrine and Susanoo Shrine were {{ill|Shrine Consolidation Policy|Q11590700|qid=Q11590700|lt=merged}}.

===Facilities===
Precinct shrines include Nijō Shrine, Ebisu Shrine, Kotohira Shrine, and Inari Shrine.

This area was formerly the hereditary land of Soga no Kurayamada no Ishikawamaro; at the shrine front is the tomb of {{ill|Ono no Imoko|Q1284072|qid=Q1284072}}, and nearby are the mausolea of {{ill|Emperor Kōtoku|Q317980|qid=Q317980}} and {{ill|Empress Suiko|Q298057|qid=Q298057}}. Also in {{ill|Eifuku-ji|Q11410732|qid=Q11410732}} in Taishi is {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shinaga-ryō}} (Shōtoku Taishi mausoleum; Eifukuji-kita kofun).
